chunks: And from him (Al-Haduth) from Ya'qub from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub Ibrahim ibn Isa, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Which type of Hajj is the most superior?' He said: 'Al-Mut'ah.' And how can anything be superior to it, while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) says: 'If I had faced from my affair what I faced at the end, I would have done as the people did.'

key_terms.الْمُتْعَةُ: Al-Mut'ah (a specific type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj with a specific contract)

ai.seo_question: What is the most superior type of Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes Hajj al-Mut'ah as the superior form of pilgrimage by referencing the Prophet’s statement: 'If I had anticipated what I later encountered, I would have done as the people did.' This implies that the Prophet originally performed Hajj al-Mut'ah (combining Umrah and Hajj without separating them) and only changed his practice due to external circumstances or the abrogation of the specific ruling, thereby marking the original form as the ideal. This narration is central to the Shia argument for the validity and superiority of Mut'ah Hajj, contrasting it with the Qiran or Ifrad practices adopted by the majority after the Prophet's later years.
